contradictions.resolution: The root makes it one thing. The mod changes a machine into an ancient machine 'that can no longer simply be researched and built like normal'; that is what onboarding does to a factory machine, and it is already true of the two vanilla machines. For every onboarded machine the Original is a fourth level 'no longer attainable through research or repair, used only for comparison'.
contradictions.text: 'The original' is two different things in the built mod. For the smelter it is an ordinary factory machine the player could have built, had the mod not hidden it: restoring it gives back what the mod took. For the power cell and the emanator it is a thing nobody can build: even a kludged one is a gift. His ruling that nothing equals the original holds for both, but the old north star's line that a refurbished machine reads 'beyond modern' is true only of the second kind and is what his ruling withdrew. The root has to say which kind the mod is about, or that it is both and why.

The bundle measured that no def names Rakatan, Utinni, Jawa or Star Wars. That is true and narrower than his ruling, which allows no setting at all. The player still reads 'the ship': 'Bring the ship's alloy forge back to heat', 'restoring wrecked ship machinery', 'The ship's water distillation module, torn off its mounts in the crash', and the three restoration projects carry the ShipRelated tag; README.md still speaks of the Kolyska. contradictions.position: His statement names the fourth level 'Original' (OWNER:1795755622961436106). The player-facing word for the top def is Original, not Repaired.

The original-grade smelter is still RM_WM_AutomatedSmelter_Repaired, labelled 'repaired automated smelter', the settings screen speaks of 'the Repaired tier', and the distillation module's top grade is 'repaired'. The Armoury, ResearchRetag and the proof scripts name the _Repaired def, so a rename touches neighbours. What the player reads is a design line for stage 3; the defName is a build detail.

contradictions.text: Study and repair pull against each other. Kludged needs no study and no research, and building it removes the wreck that the smelter's study points at; so the cheapest play is to never study at all, and a player who kludges first has nothing left to study. The mobile lines let the kludged grade be studied too; the smelter does not. The design has to say when study happens and what it buys.

His old north star opens with grades told apart at a glance. On disk the power cell's three grades share the vanilla cell picture, the emanator's three share the vanilla emanator picture, the refurbished smelter shares the original grade's picture, and the Ancient Component is a tinted vanilla component. Only the smelter's wrecked and kludged grades have a picture that no other grade uses. Until the art exists, eight of the ten machine defs share their picture with another grade, so the grade cannot be read without a click. This is the 'much larger lift in terms of art generation' he named; it is build work with an art judge, not a question.

decisions.speaker: agent
decisions.what: Feasibility, read from the game source through RimSage: the base game has a study mechanism that needs no other mod. A thing with CompProperties_CompAnalyzableUnlockResearch (canStudyInPlace, analysisRequiredRange, showProgress, progress and completion letters) is studied where it stands by JobDriver_StudyItem; a ResearchProjectDef that lists the thing in requiredAnalyzed stays locked until the study count is met, and the research screen says what is not yet studied. Progress is kept by analysisID in the game's AnalysisManager, so it outlives the wreck. Biotech's mechanitor chips use it on items; no vanilla building uses it, so one live look on a building is owed before a bar leans on it. It differs from Research Reinvented's Analyse: vanilla study opens a locked project, Research Reinvented's study fills the project's bar.

decisions.speaker: agent
decisions.what: Feasibility of a wreck that is found: three routes already work in this repo for other mods' wrecked buildings, all without new C# in this mod. (1) A prefab added to Odyssey's ancient-ruin room lists, as Cold Storage does for its wrecked stasis locker: this is his 'found at ancient ruin sites'. (2) The shared set-piece scatterer of Environmental Hazards (RM_GenStep_PlacedSetPieces), as FlowWorks uses for its wrecked water works on ordinary maps. (3) A row in Wreckage's wreck field (RM_GenStep_WreckField); its 'repairable few' weight is not built. Vanilla also scatters single ancient things on maps by a plain GenStep_ScatterThings def.

decisions.speaker: agent
decisions.what: Feasibility of 'relic value does not count toward colony wealth': the game's WealthWatcher adds each player building's MarketValueIgnoreHp into building wealth, so a Harmony patch there (the mod already carries Harmony and the shared PatchApplier) can leave the mod's machines out while they keep a trade value.

(1) Of the forge he said: 'Giving the "smelter first" is an Utinni-tier decision independent of this mod about machine availability.' The Designer's reading: the alloy forge's steps move to that tier (stage 3 writes the move with its acceptance test). (2) Of the distillation machine he said it 'is definitely a FlowWorks machine that would then be onboarded into this mod to become Wrecked if we so desired'. The Designer's reading: 0.1.0 supports only the factory mod and the vanilla items he named, so its wrecked form is a later onboarding and its working form belongs in FlowWorks. (3) He did not speak of the salvage rule. The Designer's call, which he can undo: it is not the onboarding of a machine, so it is outside the promise; it works as today, and stage 3 names its home (it is shared code already, linked only by this mod). Left for stage 2: whether a rule that waits for its move goes on working as today or is switched off until then; his first-version card says switched off, and the Armoury's durasteel is made on that forge.

decisions.speaker: agent
decisions.what: Position for stage 2, on two of his sentences that pull apart: 'found and retrieved to a safe location' (2026-11-26) and 'repairing big machines in place, and that's excellent' (2026-09-15). Reading: both hold. A wreck of any size can be taken up and carried, like the furniture-installable machine it was; the colony sets it down where it is safe; each repair is then made on the machine where it stands, with no workbench. 'In place' is where the machine stands, not where it was found. A wreck found on the colony's own map may be repaired where it lies. What the build changes: the smelter's Wrecked and Kludged grades cannot be picked up today. Whether a Kludged machine may be moved is not settled by his words; stage 2 settles it.

failure_modes: There is no way in. Nothing places a wreck in the world and nothing yields an Ancient Component, so a player never finds a machine: the ladder starts only if they build a 'wreck' from the menu for 30 steel, and it stops at Kludged. The found, surviving ancient machine he pictures never happens in a real game, however good the ladder under it is.

It reads as a building-upgrade menu, not as a machine that survived. Eight of the ten machine defs share a picture with another grade, so the grade cannot be seen; studying the wreck exists only when another mod is loaded, is never needed for the first step, and loses its subject when that step is built; and nobody has ever watched a grade being built over another by a pawn, a cell giving its trickle, or an emanator soothing anyone. The mod has been loaded, never played.

The generic mod is not generic and not one thing, so the experiment tests old debris instead of Fable. A stranger who installs it loses the factory mod's smelter from the build menu, gets the alloy forge re-gated, smelting and cremation changed and a 'ship's' distillation module, and reads about 'the ship' in a mod that promises no setting; four of our own mods lean on its names without saying so. If 0.1.0 does not draw the line around the one promise, the build spends its cycles on a red plasteel row and three untested riders, and what is left of the promise is one smelter and two vanilla machines with a number attached.

The place rule, the Refurbished grade and the full-restoration cap were written after that and never run in a game. Offline today: the kernel fuzz is green (15000 cases) on the shipped kernel file.
inventory.what: One ladder of grades for every treated machine: Wrecked, Kludged, Refurbished and the original. Each upper grade is built over a lower grade of the same machine in the same place (vanilla replaceTags plus a place rule that refuses open ground; a reinstall is free). Nothing reaches the original unless the player switches full restoration on; the capability ratios stay ordered and below the original whatever a config says. Other mods already ride this ladder by name: Cold Storage's stasis lockers, the Rakatan stasis skins in Cuisine, the Armoury's alloy recipes on the smelter grades, and ResearchRetag's research tabs.

inventory.proof_note: Wrecked and Kludged art seen live 2026-09-01; Kludged and the original grade resolved on a load 2026-11-04 (MODCHECK_DONOR_ENVIRONMENTS_1 A2). No smelter grade was ever seen smelting. Offline: validation.py static checks pass (process counts, overclock flag, research gate).
inventory.what: The automated smelter, the one factory machine treated: a dead wreck (inert, no comps, can be taken apart), a kludged smelter that runs three of the donor's six recipes, breaks down twice as often and cannot be overclocked, a refurbished one with five recipes that costs an Ancient Component and the restoration research, and the original-grade one that matches the donor machine. root.how_it_was_made: His typed answer to a_root is a statement of his own, with 'you may rephrase for efficiency or clarity', 'This is the original intention of this mod and remains true' and 'Please revise with the current version's detail while maintaining the truth of this statement'. `words` is that statement, word for word. `text` is run rm-role-designer-1795756411's rephrasing, sentence for sentence; its last sentence takes in his 'remember' sentence from the same event. `agent_words` lists each wording that is not his. A fresh Opus reader (a90c3d35ce434f40d, not the author) compared text and words; three wordings that said more than he did were taken out on its findings ('wrecked' where a machine is found, 'the machines of any mod', 'ancient vanilla machines').
root.reviewed_by: rm-judge a90c3d35ce434f40d (fresh Opus, not the author)
root.speaker: owner
root.text: Wrecked Machines changes specified machines that install like furniture, such as those of Vanilla Furniture Expanded - Factory, into advanced, ancient machines. A colony can no longer simply research and build one. A colony must find one and bring it to a safe place. Colonists study the machine, and the study opens its research. Then they repair the machine slowly, through levels of function. A Wrecked machine does not work. A Kludged machine works at a minimum. A Refurbished machine has full function, but is slower than the original. The Original is a fourth level, there only for comparison: no research and no repair reaches it. Each repair needs study of the machine, time at a research bench and considerable resources. The last repair, to Refurbished, also needs a rare Ancient Component. The idea can be applied to any game tree. This first version supports only Vanilla Furniture Expanded - Factory in this way, and some versions of vanilla expanded items such as archotech power supplies and psychic emitters.
root.words: The mod changes specified furniture-installable machines such as Vanilla Factory Enhanced into advanced, ancient machines that can no longer simply be researched and built like normal. Instead, they must be found and retrieved to a safe location, studied to enable research, and then slowly repaired through several levels of functionality: wrecked (nonfunctional), Kludged (minimal), Refurbished (full functionality but slower than original), Original (no longer attainable through research or repair, used only for comparison). Each repair requires machine study, research bench time, and considerable resources. The final refurbishment requires a rare ancient component. While the concept may be applied to any game tree, the mod's initial version will only support Vanilla Factory Enhanced in this fashion.

scope.speaker: owner
scope.text: He picked Wrecked Machines for the all-Fable build and named its shape: a generic implementation first, then a Utinni specialization (the holy aspect of repair, woven into the god-ship), possibly extended to ship components. He calls the generic one 'a good, strong concept save for the much larger lift in terms of art generation' and says it 'Needs a LOT of work using our modern Design passes'. His open question, 'whether we even bother with the generic version', is answered by the Conductor's call d_generic_is_the_mod; this design still writes the case for and against.

scope.speaker: owner
scope.text: His go for the all-Fable experiment, and the brief for this design: take the bundled tickets, 'clarify and put needed bars and tests', fan out to subagents as needed. It lifts his hold of 2026-11-19.

scope.speaker: owner
scope.text: 'Questions are welcome from the wrecked machine design phase for me in card form as needed. Let's make the design shine.' For this mod each real design choice goes to him as a card; the Conductor does not answer a Designer ask in his place.

scope.speaker: owner
scope.text: The mod stands alone at the RimMandrake level and knows nothing of god favour; the campaign layer requires it, never the reverse. The item's ruling 0 spells out the consequence: complete and playable in a vanilla game, no faction, no setting, and no setting word in a defName, label or description.

scope.speaker: owner
scope.text: 'There is nothing beyond or even equal to the original.' The ladder approaches the original and stops below it; the item's ruling 3 records that his earlier 'would exceed modern technology' is withdrawn, and that a repaired machine's value is that the colony has it at all, not that it is strong.

scope.speaker: owner
scope.text: The feel he wants: ancient machines that are still somewhat functional and lose capacity slowly instead of stopping ('Their batteries just slowly lose capacity over millenia yet still work'), and repair of big machines in place, which he called 'excellent'.

scope.speaker: owner
scope.text: The machine in front of the pawn is the research subject: 'study the MACHINE itself as part of the research' (2026-09-15), and the wreck 'should teach them about how to fix that machine… and the associated research item it is part of, slowly' (2026-08-12).

scope.speaker: owner
scope.text: Machines a colony can carry are in the mod: 'turrets, batteries, psychic emitters, and other traditionally archotech sources', a list he expects to grow ('We'll undoubtedly author more as we go on').

scope.speaker: owner
scope.text: Refurbishment costs Ancient Components, 'a truly scarce and valuable resource'. The same sentence ties the know-how to 'the ship' and promises ship auto-repair late; those two parts name a setting and belong to the layers above (d_utinni_separate, d_ship_parts_next).

scope.speaker: owner
scope.text: A found machine is an ordinary building, installed like any other; there is no socket or slot mechanism.

scope.speaker: owner
scope.text: 'remove the VFE factory, not the manual one': the donor mod's automated smelter leaves the build menu so that the wreck ladder is the road to one; vanilla's hand-run electric smelter stays.

scope.speaker: owner
scope.text: The doctrine behind the mod, said for the campaign: to repair existing broken machinery is much easier than to build it from scratch. The sentence names the ship and the clan; the generic mod keeps only the rule that repair is the easier road.

scope.speaker: owner
scope.text: 'For wrecked machines, they should ALL draw in the piping and conduit the same way, not only at a certain value of fixedness.' A wreck joins pipes and conduit visually like its repaired grades.

scope.speaker: agent
scope.text: Three rulings he took by question card on 2026-10-03, known only through the bench's note of 2026-10-04 (event 1791074563677309893; no owner event carries the card): a wrecked ancient machine can be destroyed like any building; a relic's value does not count toward colony wealth; relics are found at ancient ruin sites. Treated as his rulings; the card text itself could not be read.

scope.speaker: owner
scope.text: 'Durasteel earlier, plasteel later': the alloy forge comes early and its harder recipes unlock later. Said for the campaign's materials; the gates that carry it live in this mod's folder today (inv_alloy_forge_gates).

scope.speaker: owner
scope.text: His statement of what the mod is, given as his answer to a_root: 'This is the original intention of this mod and remains true.' It is the root. The Designer's reading, not his words, of where the statement differs from the paragraph of turn 1 and from the built mod: (1) the mod changes 'specified furniture-installable machines' into ancient machines and 'the mod's initial version will only support Vanilla Factory Enhanced in this fashion', so the turn-1 words 'any RimWorld game' are gone; (2) a wreck is 'found and retrieved to a safe location', where the built smelter wreck cannot be picked up; (3) Wrecked is 'nonfunctional', where the built power-cell wreck gives a faint current; (4) Refurbished is 'full functionality but slower than original', where the built refurbished smelter runs five of six recipes; (5) the Original is a fourth level 'used only for comparison'; (6) 'Each repair requires machine study, research bench time, and considerable resources', where the built Kludged grade needs neither study nor research; (7) the Ancient Component is 'rare' and is the price of 'The final refurbishment'.

scope.speaker: owner
scope.text: What 0.1.0 supports, in his words: 'VFE plus some versions of vanilla expanded items like archotech power supplies and psychic emitters will be the only supported options', and 'the mod's initial version will only support Vanilla Factory Enhanced in this fashion'. The Designer's readings, not his words: the mod may go on requiring the factory mod, as it does today; 'vanilla expanded items like archotech power supplies and psychic emitters' are the mod's built power cell and psychic emanator lines, which copy two base-game things; no turret and no FlowWorks machine enters in 0.1.0.

scope.speaker: owner
scope.text: 'remember: we must first prioritize Utinni service'. The Designer's reading, not his words: this is a rule for our choices and not a line that the player sees. Where 0.1.0 must choose what to do first (which machine, which level's art), it chooses what the campaign needs first; what the player reads stays free of any setting (s_standalone_no_setting).

scope.speaker: owner
scope.text: His card answer to a_how_found: 'Ruins, plus a rare wreck'. Wrecks are in ancient ruins, and now and then one half-buried wreck lies on an ordinary map on arrival; the ruins hold the good ones. Every colony meets the mod, even one that never leaves home.

scope.speaker: owner
scope.text: His answer to a_riders, which he called 'confounded'. A machine enters this mod by onboarding: 'Each machine Certainly Will need specific recipies blessed per repair tier, production rates, etc... that will be the normal onboarding process for any device into the Wrecked Machines mod.' Onboarding is by hand in 0.1.0: 'We may be able to semi-automate this to support other machines, but not in 0.1.0.' Which machine a colony gets first is not this mod's: 'Giving the "smelter first" is an Utinni-tier decision independent of this mod about machine availability.' The distillation machine is FlowWorks': 'Water Distillation is definitely a FlowWorks machine that would then be onboarded into this mod to become Wrecked if we so desired (and without this, it would remain a fully functional machine in FlowWorks).'
